key_insight: Digital motor scores from wearables map to specific striatal dopamine-denervation patterns in Parkinson’s disease, with gait showing the strongest link to frontostriatal dysfunction.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest digital assessments may help quantify and localize motor impairment in Parkinson’s disease, potentially supporting more precise monitoring of disease progression.
method: 17 Parkinson’s patients and 39 healthy controls underwent simultaneous 11C-dMP PET and resting-state fMRI.
Digital health technology was used to derive composite motor scores for arm swing, gait, and balance.
Voxel-based PET correlation and seed-based functional connectivity analyses linked motor scores to striatal and network changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports differential striatal correlations for arm swing, gait, and balance, with the most robust association seen for gait in the right caudate and anteromedial putamen, plus reduced frontostriatal connectivity.
watch_item: Small sample size and preliminary cross-sectional design limit generalizability and do not establish causality or clinical deployment readiness.
paper_title: Striatal representations and network correlates of digital motor scores in Parkinsons disease
